lines.arrive: A lecture, on the shape of the world.
lines.ladder: There's a ladder, over the edge of the world.
lines.turtle_1: A turtle. A very large one.
lines.turtle_look: It looks up at you, slowly, and goes back to holding up the world.
lines.ask: So what holds the world up? And what holds that up?
lines.forever: You could go on like this forever. Every turtle needs another one under it.
lines.curve: The stack isn't quite straight. Far below, it curves away, very slightly.
lines.down_2: There's always another turtle. The chain never ends. But it never quite explains itself, either.
lines.last_1: This one stands on nothing at all. It just does.
lines.last_2: The chain has to stop somewhere, some say, at something that needs nothing underneath it. But why here? Why this one?
lines.loop_1: The turtles go round in a great ring, each on the back of the one before. The last one holds up the first.
lines.loop_2: There's no bottom, because there's no bottom to reach. They hold each other up.
lines.stop_2: Most people do, most of the time. The world stays up either way.
